statements.t: The South Texas Divestiture substantially achieved our target of selling more than $1.0 billion in assets within one year of the completion of the Merger, which has enabled us to reduce debt and strengthen our capital structure.
We expect additional pipeline capacity to come online during the remainder of 2026 to further support takeaway out of the Permian Basin.

• We substantially completed the integration of the Merger across all key operational and organizational workstreams and have captured targeted synergies from our combined operations, with remaining integration activities expected to continue in the normal course.
Our capital program for 2026 is expected to be approximately $2.75 billion, excluding acquisitions.

We remain focused on applying our strength in geosciences and development optimization to highly economic oil and liquids-rich development projects in our areas of operations that support our priority of strategic inventory replacement and growth.
Refer to Overview of Liquidity and Capital Resources below for discussion of how we expect to fund the remainder of our 2026 capital program.
We anticipate operating an average of six drilling rigs and an average of one completion crew for the remainder of 2026.
We anticipate operating an average of one drilling rig for the remainder of 2026 and one completion crew for a portion of the fourth quarter of 2026.
We anticipate operating one drilling rig and no completion crews for the remainder of 2026.
We anticipate operating an average of three drilling rigs and one completion crew during the remainder of 2026.

The volume of our expected production that we cover with commodity derivative contracts is determined by our balance sheet objectives, capital allocation priorities, anticipated development activity and associated capital requirements, and prevailing commodity market conditions, including available future prices and derivative structures.

The Merger, which closed on January 30, 2026, and the South Texas Divestiture, which closed on April 30, 2026, have materially affected our operating and financial results and will continue to affect comparability with prior periods.

For the full-year 2026, we expect LOE per BOE to increase compared with 2025, driven by the inclusion of higher-cost acquired assets and a shift in production mix across our assets following the South Texas Divestiture.
We expect to realize operational and cost synergies which will partially offset this increase.

We anticipate volatility in LOE per BOE as a result of changes in geographic and commodity mix of our production, timing of workover projects, changes in service provider costs, integration-related activities and broader industry conditions, all of which affect total LOE.

We expect transportation costs to vary based on production volumes and commodity mix, contractual transportation agreements, applicable rates, and the utilization of transportation capacity across our operating areas.
On a per BOE basis, we expect transportation costs for 2026 to decrease slightly compared with 2025.
We generally expect our Uinta Basin and South Texas assets to incur lower production tax rates compared with our Permian and DJ Basin assets.

We anticipate volatility in ad valorem tax expense on a per BOE and absolute basis due to varying tax policies and assessment methodologies across the counties in which we operate, changes in our commodity and production mix across our assets, and fluctuations in commodity prices.
For the full-year 2026, we expect DD&A expense on an absolute basis to increase compared with 2025 due to higher production volumes, while we expect DD&A expense to decrease on a per BOE basis.

For the full-year 2026, we expect G&A expense on an absolute basis to increase compared with 2025, primarily due to an increase in employee headcount as a result of the Merger, and one-time integration costs, a majority of which were incurred during the first half of 2026.

We expect increases in benchmark commodity prices to result in net derivative losses and decreases in benchmark commodity prices to result in net derivative gains, as measured against our derivative contract prices.

Our effective tax rate for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, reflects the proportional effects of forecast net income on estimated permanent items between periods and state apportionment factors affecting the allocation of taxable income across jurisdictions with varying statutory tax rates.
Our IRC Section 382 analysis and state tax planning indicate that certain tax attributes are expected to be utilized in 2026.

Based on our current liquidity position, anticipated operating cash flows, and available sources of capital, we believe we have sufficient financial resources to execute our business plan and meet our short-term and long-term financial obligations, including maturities of our outstanding Senior Notes.

For the remainder of 2026, we expect to fund our capital expenditures and return of capital program with cash flows from operations, with any remaining cash needs being funded by borrowings under our revolving credit facility.
Although we expect cash flows from these sources to be sufficient for the remainder of 2026, we may also elect to raise funds through new debt or equity offerings or from other sources of financing.
We expect our weighted-average interest rate and weighted-average borrowing rate to increase slightly for the full-year 2026 compared with 2025.

We periodically review our capital expenditure budget and guidance to assess if changes are necessary based on current and projected cash flows, acquisition and divestiture activities, debt requirements, and other factors.

Under our stockholder return framework announced in February 2026, we currently target approximately 20 percent of free cash flow, calculated on a quarterly basis and after dividend payments, for share repurchases, with the potential to repurchase in excess of this level as we continue to execute on our strategy and bolster our balance sheet.

We currently intend to continue paying dividends to our stockholders for the foreseeable future, subject to our future earnings, our financial condition, covenants under our Credit Agreement and the indentures governing our Senior Notes, and other factors that could arise.

statements.t: In the third quarter, the Company substantially completed its Civitas merger (the “Merger”) integration and exceeded targeted run-rate synergies, transitioning the business to continuous improvement.

SM Energy President and CEO Beth McDonald said, “We are meaningfully transforming SM Energy – exceeding our merger synergy target, substantially achieving our divestiture target and materially strengthening the balance sheet.
We are modestly lowering full-year oil guidance to 220-222 MBbl/d due to transitory factors, while reiterating our full-year total production outlook.
Importantly, despite service-cost inflation, we now expect 2026 capital of approximately $2.75 billion, the midpoint of our prior range, supported by synergy capture and ongoing efficiency gains.
We expect the factors leading to our lower oil production outlook to be resolved in early 2027.
We remain on track for low one-times leverage at mid-cycle prices by year-end 2026, strengthening the capacity for durable stockholder returns.
The Permian factors that affected third-quarter volumes have been addressed, and we expect the Uinta takeaway constraints to be resolved in early 2027.
• Included in our oil volume guidance is a continued impact from takeaway constraints in the Uinta Basin.

Capital expenditures : The Company’s operating plan guidance uses the term “capital expenditures,” which is defined to be before changes in accruals (excludes working capital), and is a non-GAAP measure.

dropped.t: SM Energy Company (the “ Company ”) is providing the following summary of earnings considerations that management believes will impact results for the third quarter of 2026.
For the third quarter of 2026, the Company anticipates a net derivative settlement loss of $207 million.

This amount reflects settlements of commodity derivatives during the quarter and excludes changes in the fair value of unsettled derivative positions, which could be material and will be reported with the Company’s third quarter results.

These statements include, without limitation, statements regarding commodity prices, realized prices, derivative activity, market conditions, anticipated financial results and other factors affecting the Company’s results of operations.
